title.narrative: Provision of life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable communities in under-served hard-to-reach rural areas in Dinsor District through provision of preventive and curative nutrition services.

description.narrative: ltpgtDMO proposes a 12-month integrated nutrition program targeting Diinsoor District in Bay Region, Somalia. The intervention will focus on seven underserved villages: Dinsoor Health Facility/OTP/SC. Holwadag, Village) Korka Mari IDP (Outreach OTP), Section siinay ), Tuur Waluun IDP Outreach OTP) section October ) Waaberi Villages section Haawo tako Outreach OTP) One fixed sites, are Waabeiri and Dinsoor Health Facility, will Four OTP locations, including Dinsoor Health Facility also hosting the Stabilization Centre for complicated SAM cases. SAM cases without medical complications will be treated at the two fixed OTP sites, while complicated cases will be referred to the SC in Dinsoor. Children and PLW with MAM will be referred to partner-operated TSFP. CHWs, deployed two per village, will conduct regular biweekly door-to-door screenings using MUAC tapes and oedema checks, actively promoting the Family MUAC approach. CHWs will also be responsible for follow-up of referred children to ensure admission and adherence to treatment.ltbrgtNutrition treatment supplies including RUTF, therapeutic milk, and routine medications will be provided by UNICEF under the signed PCA with DMO. Children admitted to the SC will also receive routine immunization in accordance with the Somalia EPI schedule, delivered in coordination with the health partner operating within the facility. Deworming and Vitamin A supplementation will be provided both at facility and community levels, including during mass screening campaigns, targeting 5,090 children with Vitamin A and 3,090 children with dewormers. MNP will be distributed to 1,700 children aged 6 to 23 months receiving it for the first time, while 1,400 PLW will receive MMS or iron folate supplements during ANC and PNC linked nutrition visits.ltbrgtThe program will promote SBCC through MIYCAN and IYCF initiatives. DMO will train 28 nutrition staff on MIYCAN and 14 CHWs on IYCF, integrating cross-cutting topics such as child protection, GBV risk mitigation and referral, AAP, and PDAD. These messages will be cascaded to caregivers through biweekly household visits, support group meetings, and community dialogues. The project will establish 35 MTMSGs comprising women of reproductive age, who will be trained using Somali IEC materials and MUAC tapes to serve as SBCC agents in their communities. Cooking demonstrations, 35 in total, will be held across all villages, focusing on locally appropriate meals, the Tom Brown porridge approach, and the One Egg Per Day campaign to improve dietary diversity and nutritional intake in young children.ltbrgtTo ensure equitable access and inclusive participation, DMO will conduct targeted mapping to identify marginalized and minority groups within the intervention villages . A robust framework will be established to monitor and report on the inclusion of minority groups, utilizing sex, age, and vulnerability disaggregated data and regular assessments to track progress and participation. The project will also strengthen feedback mechanisms to ensure accessibility through multiple platforms and inclusive language. DMO will prioritize the recruitment of minority staff to reflect community diversity and ensure that their voices are represented in program design and delivery. Monthly monitoring visits will be led by the DMO Project Manager and MEAL team, using standard OTP supervision checklists and supporting data quality checks. Six supportive supervision and on-the-job training sessions will be conducted across the two OTP sites to ensure quality service delivery and mentoring of frontline staff. Where feasible, MoH officials will participate in the supervision activities. The project will be implemented in close coordination with the Area-Based Coordination Group, the MoH, and local community structures. Community engagement will form a cornerstone of the approach, ensuring local ownership, participation, and sustainability of interventions throughout Diinsoor District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
